findings.evidence: loadAssignedAttemptForUpdate() locked only ExamAttempt then separately read the lazy exam.getProctorId() afterward, unlocked — a concurrent unassignProctor() could race an in-flight proctor action, violating the CRITICAL 'authorization atomic with state change' constraint.
findings.why_it_matters: A revoked proctor assignment mid-action could still land a mutation if the authorization read happened before the revocation committed.
findings.required_action: Combine lock acquisition and authorization into one query: findByIdAndAssignedProctorForUpdate(id, proctorId) with the proctor check in the WHERE clause under PESSIMISTIC_WRITE, so the join locks both ExamAttempt and Exam rows atomically.

findings.evidence: proctor_action table (backing a BaseEntity-extending JPA entity) was missing updated_at/is_deleted columns that BaseEntity requires, relying implicitly on ddl-auto=update to paper over the gap.
findings.why_it_matters: Deployments with stricter ddl-auto settings (validate/none) would fail; contradicts this codebase's established explicit-migration pattern.
findings.required_action: Add updated_at and is_deleted columns matching BaseEntity's contract.

findings.evidence: Pre-existing bug from Phase 7 (already quality-approved): the proctor table used a column literally named 'deleted' instead of BaseEntity's actual @Column(name = "is_deleted") mapping — would have produced an orphaned unused column alongside a Hibernate-auto-created is_deleted column under ddl-auto=update.
findings.why_it_matters: Same root cause as QUAL-002; fixed opportunistically while touching the same area, since the migration hadn't been run against any real database yet (safe to edit in place, not a destructive change to an already-applied migration).
findings.required_action: None — corrected to is_deleted while fixing QUAL-002.
